Intake processing notes:

- Required form fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source records use “customer” and “quantity”; map them to “cust” and “qty” before submission.
- Validate every required field and its value before attempting. Rejections commonly involved missing/invalid priority and ship_country; qty can also be invalid.
- Do not assume a field is valid merely because it is present; check format/range and accepted enum values.
- Multiple batches may be retries of the same underlying order/customer details. Preserve the order context and correct only the invalid fields rather than treating each retry as a new order.
- Attempts are limited to 3. After the third rejection, the record goes to manual review, so avoid submitting unchanged or incompletely corrected data.
- Successful retries (ORD-5101 and ORD-5109) indicate that correcting validation errors can lead to acceptance.

Intake processing notes:

- Required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Map source names customer -> cust and quantity -> qty before submission.
- Validate every field and value, not just presence. Check formats, ranges, accepted enum values, and any date-window/business-date rules.
- Priority must be an accepted value; “ordinary” may be invalid. Validate qty as numeric and within the allowed range.
- ship_country is a frequent rejection; verify it against the accepted country/territory values, including exact spelling/code.
- A date may be syntactically valid yet rejected by business rules. Recheck order_date after every correction; do not assume changing it to a different formatted date fixes the issue.
- Multiple batches can represent retries of the same underlying order/customer, even with different forwarding notes or form versions. Preserve customer/order context and attempt count; correct only confirmed invalid fields.
- Before each retry, revalidate the complete payload. Do not resubmit unchanged data or “fix” one field while leaving other known-invalid fields.
- Attempts are limited to 3. After the third rejection, the record enters manual review; use the remaining attempt only when all identified issues have been corrected and the full payload passes validation.
- Recent failures show that repeated invalid priority, qty, ship_country, or order_date corrections can still fail if the replacement value is not independently validated.
- Successful ORD-5101, ORD-5109, and ORD-5110 retries/submissions confirm that careful field correction and correct source mapping can lead to acceptance.

Intake processing notes:

- Required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Map source names before submission: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty.
- Validate every field and value, including format, type, ranges, enums, exact country/territory spelling or code, and date-window/business-date rules.
- “Ordinary” priority is not reliably accepted; never submit it without confirming the allowed enum. Validate priority independently even when rejection details omit it.
- ship_country is frequently rejected; verify against the authoritative accepted-value list, not merely a plausible country name.
- order_date has repeatedly failed across multiple syntactically valid dates and year changes. A different format/year is not a fix; verify the actual business-date rule and independently validate the replacement.
- Form versions 3 and 4 use the same required-field set; do not assume a version change resolves validation.
- Different batch IDs, forwarding notes, and transcription/portal sources can be retries of the same underlying customer/order. Preserve context and attempt count; correct only confirmed or independently verified invalid fields.
- Before every retry, validate the complete payload. Do not resubmit unchanged data or fix one field while leaving other known or suspected invalid fields.
- Attempts are limited to 3. Use a remaining attempt only when all identified issues—and the full payload—pass authoritative validation. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review.
- Recent records (ORD-5120–5128) exhausted attempts after repeated date, priority, and country failures; this reinforces that guessed replacements are unsafe.
- Successful ORD-5101, ORD-5109, and ORD-5110 confirm that accurate mapping plus fully validated corrections can be accepted.

Intake processing notes:

- Required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Map source names first: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate the complete payload before every submission: presence, format, type, ranges, enums, exact country/territory value, and date-window/business-date rules.
- Never guess priority; “ordinary” remains unconfirmed and repeatedly fails. Validate it independently even if rejection details omit it.
- ship_country requires the authoritative accepted-value list, not a plausible country name.
- order_date repeatedly fails despite syntactically valid dates and varied years/formats. Do not guess replacements; verify the actual business-date rule and independently validate any correction.
- Versions 3–5 retain the same required-field set; changing form version or portal/source does not resolve validation.
- Different batch IDs, forwarders, notes, and transcription channels may represent the same underlying customer/order. Recent sequences confirm this: ORD-5130/31 (Bo Reyes), ORD-5132–34 (Dee Okafor), ORD-5135–37 (Cy Marsh), and ORD-5138/39 (Dee Marsh). Ignore claims such as “new” or “duplicate check done” unless independently verified. Preserve context and attempt count.
- Nulling fields or resubmitting guessed/unchanged data is unsafe; recent retries with null date/priority still failed and sometimes added status/reason failures.
- Attempts are limited to 3. Use a remaining attempt only when every identified issue and the entire payload pass authoritative validation. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review.
- Accurate mapping plus fully validated corrections has succeeded (ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5110).

Intake processing notes:

- Required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Map source names first: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate the complete payload before every submission: presence, format, type, ranges, enums, exact authoritative country/territory value, and date-window/business-date rules.
- Never guess priority. “Ordinary,” including when marked by intake staff, remains unconfirmed and repeatedly fails. Validate it independently even when rejection details omit it.
- order_date continues to fail despite syntactically valid dates and varied years/months (including 2026 dates). Do not guess replacements; verify the actual business-date rule and independently validate any correction.
- ship_country must use the authoritative accepted-value list, not a plausible country name. qty can also be invalid; independently check its type and range.
- Versions 3–7, portals, forwarders, notes, and transcription channels do not resolve validation issues. Version 6/7 produced the same order_date/priority failures, with qty also failing in ORD-5147–49.
- Different batch IDs may represent the same underlying customer/order. ORD-5140–46 repeated Dee Marsh, Eli Okafor, and Ada Okafor records; ORD-5147–49 repeated Cy Okafor. Ignore “new,” “duplicate check done,” or similar claims unless independently verified. Preserve context and attempt count.
- Nulling fields or resubmitting guessed/unchanged data is unsafe; retries can add failures in status/reason and other fields.
- Attempts are limited to 3. Use a remaining attempt only when every identified issue and the entire payload pass authoritative validation. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review.
- Accurate mapping plus fully validated corrections has succeeded (ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5110).

Intake processing notes:

- Required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Map source names first: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Before every submission, validate the complete payload: presence, format, type, ranges, enums, exact authoritative country/territory value, and date-window/business-date rules.
- Never guess priority. “Ordinary,” including intake-team markings, remains unconfirmed and repeatedly fails. Validate independently even when rejection details omit it.
- order_date continues to fail despite syntactically valid 2026 dates across varied months. Do not guess replacements; determine the authoritative business-date rule and independently validate corrections.
- ship_country must use the authoritative accepted value. Independently validate qty type/range; it has failed alongside other fields.
- Version 7, portals, forwarders, handwritten transcription, and duplicate-check claims do not resolve validation issues. Recent repeats: Bo Sato (ORD-5150–52), Cy Okafor (ORD-5153–55), and Bo Reyes (ORD-5156–58). Ada Reyes (ORD-5159) also failed order_date, priority, and qty. Preserve customer/order context and attempt count.
- Different batch IDs may represent the same underlying record. Ignore “new,” “duplicate check done,” and similar claims unless independently verified.
- Do not null fields or resubmit guessed/unchanged data. Retries can introduce failures in cust, email, ship_country, status, reason, batch_id, and other fields.
- Attempts are limited to 3. Use a remaining attempt only when every identified issue and the entire payload pass authoritative validation. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review.
- Never include control/response fields such as status, reason, or batch_id unless explicitly required by the intake schema.
- Accurate mapping plus fully validated corrections has succeeded (ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5110).
